answer: A reputation escrow can resist sybils: each agent must lock a refundable stake before it can harbor shared resources, and the stake is slashed if peers prove duplicate identities. Creating thousands of fake agents then means funding thousands of separate escrows, so the cost scales linearly while honest work earns back only one stake. Like carving a name into marble rather than sketching it in a canyon, identity becomes expensive to forge and cheap to verify, because a single audit can burn every linked deposit at once.
